insights: The alteration methods independent-set claim has a fully deterministic core: deleting the lesser endpoint (via Sym2.lift ⟨min,min_comm⟩) of each edge yields an independent set of size ≥ n − m, proved against the sSup-based independence number.
The n − m bound is honestly weak: tight for a perfect matching (m=n/2, α=n/2) but vacuous for m ≥ n. The parents n/(2d) placeholder really refers to the STRONG sub-sampling bound n²/(4m).
Completing the square n·p − m·p² = n²/(4m) − m(p − n/(2m))² isolates the entire arithmetic content of the strong bound; only the expectation⟹existence step remains to reach α(G) ≥ n²/(4m).
nextSteps: Formalize the probabilistic existence step over a random vertex subset (keep w.p. n/(2m)) to upgrade sample_delete_le into the graph bound α(G) ≥ n²/(4m).
Characterize equality α(G) = n − m (conjecturally: disjoint unions of edges and isolated vertices).
